{"id":"mimid-1wgh.114.2","title":"A JMAP VTC capability on the agent, so a client can hold a keyed call","description":"Route (b) of decision mimid-1wgh.114. The half the keying is for.

WHAT IT IS: a capability on the agent's own loopback JMAP endpoint that
lets a client start a call in a chat, learn there is one, and fetch the
call room's media secret for the epoch it is in. The client runs the
media layer's key schedule over that secret, per
draft-atwood-mimi-calls §4.3, and does the media itself. mimid ships no
media stack and no UI (decision mimid-1wgh.38).

WHAT IT SITS ON, all built (bead mimid-1wgh.108): Store::start_call,
Store::media_secret, Room::parent, and the hub's room-policy-04 §5
enforcement.

THE BOUNDARY: the agent's loopback HTTP endpoint with a bearer credential
(docs/design/frontend-auth.md §3), the same one that already carries
plaintext. The secret itself is a MediaSecret: redacted Debug, zeroized
on drop, never written to the database (crates/mimid-agent-core/src/media.rs).
What has NO answer yet is what the JSON looks like, how often a client
may ask, and what it may ask for: one epoch's secret for one room it is
in, and nothing else, is the obvious shape but is not decided.

NEEDS MARK, two things, before the method names exist:
- whether this extends draft-atwood-jmap-vtc or is written fresh. That
  draft already treats a call's chatId as OPTIONAL, which decision
  mimid-1wgh.113 leaned on, so it is the natural home.
- whether the capability is on by default. Every other agent front end
  defaults to loopback, and the JMAP one is on by default; a capability
  that hands out key material may want to be opt-in.

AND REMEMBER: no JMAP goes to the MIMI working group (memory
no-jmap-to-the-mimi-wg). draft-atwood-mimi-calls says where the secret
comes from; it does not and must not mention this surface.

new_value: {"notes":"THE DOCUMENT IS DECIDED: mimid-1wgh.118, extend draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00.md. It is 2394 lines and already complete as an object model; it leaves the E2EE mechanism to the media layer by design, and jmap-vtc-e2ee-guide.md §3 already names MLS as the group key-management answer. What must be added is only the bridge: how a VTCCall relates to a MIMI call room, and how a client gets media_secret. Every write to ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec needs Mark's own OK, one per write. Still open: whether the capability is on by default."}
